tenant-placement.metaDescription: Full-cycle tenant placement across India: listing launch, marketing, showings, screening, lease execution, and move-in. Zero upfront cost, success fee on placement.
tenant-placement.heroLede: From the first listing photo to the move-in inspection, Housing365 runs the entire placement workflow for your unit. You see every showing, application, and screening decision in the portal - and you only pay a success fee when the lease is signed.
tenant-placement.problemTitle: What goes wrong without a structured placement process

problemPoints.title: Mispriced listings sit vacant
problemPoints.body: Owners who guess at asking rent either leave money on the table or over-price and watch the unit sit for six-to-eight weeks. Either outcome costs a full month of rent in the Indian rental market.

problemPoints.title: Photos and copy that do not convert
problemPoints.body: Phone photos, no floor plan, and generic listing copy get buried in the Housing.com & 99acres feeds. You end up paying for showings that never happen.

problemPoints.title: Unscreened applicants slip through
problemPoints.body: Without documented credit, employment, and reference checks, owners sign leases on faith - and find out the mistake at month three, when rent stops arriving.

problemPoints.title: Paperwork gaps invite legal tenancy risk
problemPoints.body: Missing riders, un-initialed addenda, or the wrong lease form can undo your position at the Rent Authority & Tenancy Tribunal before the tenancy even starts.

tenant-placement.solutionLede: One full-service team runs strategic pricing, listing production, showings, screening, offer negotiation, lease execution, and move-in coordination on a single timeline. You approve the decisions that matter and delegate everything else.

scope.title: Strategic pricing & listing launch
scope.body: Market-rent analysis against live comps in your PIN code, recommended asking range, and a launch plan keyed to the weekend showing cycle.

scope.title: Professional marketing
scope.body: Wide-angle photography, virtual tour, floor plan, and editorial copy syndicated to National Property Network, Housing.com & 99acres, Housing.com, 99acres, MagicBricks, and verified social channels, and the Housing365 portal.

scope.title: Coordinated showings
scope.body: Showings booked, confirmed, and hosted by licensed representatives. Every attendee is logged and every inquiry is answered within one business hour.

scope.title: Structured applicant qualification
scope.body: Credit pull, income verification, employment verification, landlord references, and a written risk summary - documented and shareable on request.

scope.title: Offer management
scope.body: Offer ingestion, counter-offer workflow, and owner approval logged in the portal. No text-message chaos, no lost thread.

scope.title: Lease execution
scope.body: Province-compliant lease (Legal e-stamped tenancy agreement), riders, deposits, and first-month rent collected on signing via e-signature.

scope.title: Move-in coordination
scope.body: Key handover, utility transfer reminders, move-in inspection report, and tenant onboarding - all closed out before day one of the tenancy.

howItWorks.title: Discovery & engagement
howItWorks.body: Twenty-minute discovery call, unit walkthrough or virtual tour, and a signed leasing engagement agreement. No upfront cost.

howItWorks.title: Pricing & prep
howItWorks.body: Market rent set, prep punch-list agreed, photography and virtual tour produced, and listing copy approved by you.

howItWorks.title: Launch
howItWorks.body: Listing syndicated across every major rental channel the same day. Inquiries routed to our leasing team and logged in your portal.

howItWorks.title: Showings & applications
howItWorks.body: Showings hosted, applications collected, and every applicant screened against a consistent rubric.

howItWorks.title: Offer & approval
howItWorks.body: Qualified applicants presented with a risk summary. You approve, counter, or decline in the portal.

howItWorks.title: Lease & move-in
howItWorks.body: Lease executed, deposits collected, keys handed over, and move-in inspection filed. Success fee invoiced on placement.

Owners of five-to-fifty units who want consistent placement quality across their book without staffing an in-house leasing team.
New-build owners leasing one or two units at close - Housing365 handles the first tenancy end-to-end and hands a clean file to your property manager.

faqItems.question: How much does tenant placement cost?
faqItems.answer: Nothing upfront. You pay a single success fee when the lease is signed, typically equal to one month of the new rent. There are no retainers, no photo fees, no screening fees, and no charges if the unit does not lease.

faqItems.question: How long does placement usually take?
faqItems.answer: Most India listings reach a signed lease within roughly two-to-four weeks of launch when priced to the live market. Homes priced above comp tend to take longer; we will flag that before we list.

faqItems.question: Do you handle rent collection after move-in?
faqItems.answer: Rent collection and ongoing property management are outside the placement scope. Placement closes when the lease is signed, deposits are collected, and the move-in inspection is filed. We can refer you to trusted property managers if you need one.

faqItems.question: What happens if the tenant breaks the lease early?
faqItems.answer: The success fee is earned on placement. If a tenancy ends early for reasons outside the screening file, you can engage Housing365 for a re-list at a reduced re-leasing rate - details are in your engagement letter.

faqItems.question: Who writes the lease?
faqItems.answer: In India, we use the e-stamped rent agreement of Lease (Form 2229E) plus owner-approved riders for parking, utilities, pets, and additional terms. All documents are signed electronically and stored in your portal.

faqItems.question: Can I reject an applicant you bring forward?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You have final say on every applicant. We present a documented risk summary with every application; you approve, counter, or decline. We follow the India Human Rights Code on every decision.

faqItems.question: Do you coordinate property prep (painting, cleaning, photos)?
faqItems.answer: Yes - that is our Rental Preparation service. It is optional and billed separately from placement. We can quote prep on the walkthrough call.

faqItems.question: Do I need to meet applicants in person?
faqItems.answer: No. Showings are hosted by our team, applications are collected in the portal, and the lease is signed electronically. You can stay as hands-off or as involved as you want.

tenant-screening.title: Tenant Screening
tenant-screening.metaDescription: Structured tenant screening in India: credit, income, employment, references, compliance. Decision-ready reports for landlords. Available standalone or bundled.
tenant-screening.heroHeadline: Applicants qualified on a written rubric
tenant-screening.heroLede: Every applicant runs through the same documented screen - credit, income, employment, references, risk assessment, and compliance checks. You get a decision-ready report in your portal, not a gut feeling on a phone call.
tenant-screening.problemTitle: What goes wrong without structured screening

problemPoints.title: Inconsistent decisions, exposure to discrimination claims
problemPoints.body: Owners who screen ad-hoc end up applying different standards to different applicants - a direct path to an India Human Rights Code complaint.

problemPoints.title: Missed red flags
problemPoints.body: Credit alone is not a tenancy decision. Without employment verification and landlord references, the applicant with a clean credit report can still be the applicant who broke the last lease.

problemPoints.title: Paper trails you cannot defend at the Rent Authority
problemPoints.body: If a tenancy sours, your screening file is the document that protects you. "I had a good feeling about them" is not a defence.

problemPoints.title: Slow screening loses the best applicants
problemPoints.body: The strongest applicants have options. A 72-hour screening turnaround loses them to the building across the street.

tenant-screening.solutionLede: A consistent, documented screen run by trained leasing staff. Every applicant gets the same checks in the same order, and every decision is logged with a written rationale - whether you engage us end-to-end or only for screening.

scope.title: Credit check
scope.body: Equifax soft-pull credit report with score, trade-line history, collections, and any judgments or bankruptcies.

scope.title: Income verification
scope.body: Pay stubs, T4s, notices of assessment, or bank-statement verification cross-checked against stated employment.

scope.title: Employment verification
scope.body: Direct employer confirmation of role, tenure, and stated income - documented in the screening file.

scope.title: Reference verification
scope.body: Prior landlord references with structured questions on payment history, notice, and condition of the unit at move-out.

scope.title: Risk summary
scope.body: A written one-page summary that maps the applicant against your rent-to-income threshold and flags anything that needs a conversation.

scope.title: Compliance checks
scope.body: ID verification and India Human Rights Code compliance review on every decision.

scope.title: Decision support
scope.body: Our team walks you through the summary and options: approve, approve with guarantor, counter, or decline with documented reason.

howItWorks.body: Applicant fills a structured application in the portal - ID, employment, income, references, consent.

howItWorks.title: Credit & ID pull
howItWorks.body: Equifax report and ID verification run within one business hour of a complete submission.

howItWorks.title: Income & employment verification
howItWorks.body: Pay stubs, T4s, and direct employer confirmation reviewed within 24 hours.

howItWorks.title: Reference calls
howItWorks.body: Prior landlord references contacted and logged.

howItWorks.title: Risk summary written
howItWorks.body: One-page summary, risk flags, and recommended decision delivered to your portal.

howItWorks.title: Owner decision
howItWorks.body: You approve, counter, decline, or request a guarantor - all in the portal with a documented reason.

whoItsFor.fitNote: Owners who have a tenant identified and want a defensible file before signing - not just a credit score.
Owners who want a consistent rubric applied across every applicant, every unit, every month.
New-build operators who need an auditable screen on every first-tenancy applicant for investor or lender reporting.

tenant-screening.pricingNote: Included in the full Leasing Services engagement at no extra charge. Available standalone at a flat per-applicant rate - see the pricing page.

faqItems.question: Can I use your screening without the full placement engagement?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Tenant Screening is available as a standalone service at a flat per-applicant rate. You bring the applicant; we deliver the documented screen and risk summary.

faqItems.question: How long does screening take?
faqItems.answer: Typical turnaround is 24-to-48 hours from a complete application. Credit and ID usually clear within one business hour; employment and reference calls take the rest.

faqItems.question: What credit report do you pull?
faqItems.answer: Equifax soft-pull, which returns score, trade lines, collections, and public records without affecting the applicant's credit.

faqItems.question: What if the applicant does not meet income thresholds?
faqItems.answer: We can route to our Tenant Guarantor process - a structured path that adds a qualified co-signer to the lease with separate documentation.

faqItems.question: Do you make the rent or decline decision?
faqItems.answer: No. You make every final decision. Housing365 delivers the documented file and a recommendation; the owner approves, counters, or declines.

faqItems.question: Is the screening compliant with India Human Rights Code?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Our rubric screens on financial and tenancy factors only. Protected-ground factors (family status, age, source of income, etc.) do not enter the decision.

faqItems.question: Do you screen co-applicants and guarantors the same way?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Every person on the lease - tenant, co-tenant, or guarantor - runs through the same documented screen.

faqItems.question: Can I see the actual credit report?
faqItems.answer: You see the summary and the relevant risk flags. Full credit reports are retained under Equifax terms of use; applicants receive a copy on request.

rent-guarantee.title: Rent Guarantee
rent-guarantee.metaDescription: Rental protection and rent guarantee pathways for Indian landlords and property owners. Partner-underwritten coverage for non-payment and tenant default. Coordinated by Housing365.
rent-guarantee.heroLede: Housing365 coordinates partner-underwritten rent guarantee policies, tenant insurance coordination, and financial qualification validation - so a missed rent cheque does not become a missed mortgage payment. Coverage options are provided by licensed insurance partners; Housing365 handles the qualification and integration with your lease.
rent-guarantee.problemTitle: What goes wrong without rental protection

problemPoints.title: One non-paying tenant erases a year of margin
problemPoints.body: A single extended default at the Rent Authority & Tenancy Tribunal can cost six-to-nine months of rent plus legal fees - enough to wipe out the annual return on a condo unit.

problemPoints.title: Self-insuring is a gamble
problemPoints.body: Most individual landlords carry no protection against non-payment. The assumption is "it will not happen to me" - until it does.

problemPoints.title: Insurance products are hard to compare
problemPoints.body: Rent guarantee is a niche product with varying exclusions, waiting periods, and coverage caps. Shopping it solo eats hours and ends in confusion.

problemPoints.title: Policy terms do not line up with the lease
problemPoints.body: A policy that requires a specific screening standard, a specific lease form, or a specific notice period is worthless if your lease does not match.

rent-guarantee.solutionLede: Housing365 evaluates the applicant against partner rent guarantee underwriting criteria, aligns your lease with the policy requirements, and coordinates issuance. The policy is underwritten by a licensed insurance partner; Housing365 is the coordinator, not the insurer.

scope.title: Underwriting eligibility review
scope.body: We map the applicant's screening file against the partner's underwriting rubric - credit band, income ratio, employment stability - before you agree to the policy.

scope.title: Policy option presentation
scope.body: Coverage terms, monthly premium, waiting period, exclusions, and claim mechanics explained in plain language before purchase.

scope.title: Lease alignment
scope.body: Lease and riders adjusted to match policy requirements - notice clauses, tenant insurance clause, rent due date, and default language.

scope.title: Tenant insurance coordination

scope.title: Financial qualification validation

scope.body: Policy documents stored in your portal alongside the lease; renewal reminders issued before expiry.

scope.title: Claims coordination
scope.body: If a default occurs, we help you assemble the claim documentation - screening file, lease, notice of default, Rent Authority filing - so the partner can assess quickly.

whoItsFor.fitNote: Owners of one or two units where a single non-paying tenant would materially affect cash flow.
Owners of multi-unit portfolios who want predictable income and are willing to trade a small premium for default protection.

rent-guarantee.pricingNote: Housing365 does not charge extra to coordinate rent guarantee when bundled with Leasing Services. Policy premiums are set by the insurance partner and disclosed before binding.

faqItems.question: Is Housing365 the insurer?
faqItems.answer: No. Rent guarantee policies are underwritten by licensed Indian insurance partners. Housing365 coordinates qualification, policy selection, lease alignment, and claim support, but is not the insurer.

faqItems.question: How much does rent guarantee cost?
faqItems.answer: Premiums vary by coverage amount, waiting period, and applicant profile. Typical monthly premiums fall in a defined range of monthly rent; the partner will quote exactly before you bind.

faqItems.question: What does the policy cover?
faqItems.answer: Most policies cover lost rent during default up to a defined cap (commonly six months) and some legal costs of the Rent Authority process. Exclusions, waiting periods, and caps are disclosed in the policy document.

faqItems.question: Can every applicant be covered?
faqItems.answer: No. Coverage requires the applicant to meet the partner's underwriting criteria - typically a credit band and a rent-to-income ratio. We map this before you agree to the policy.

faqItems.question: Does rent guarantee replace tenant insurance?
faqItems.answer: No. Tenant insurance covers the tenant's contents and liability. Rent guarantee covers the landlord's rent income. We coordinate both as part of lease execution.

faqItems.question: What happens if the tenant defaults?
faqItems.answer: You issue the required notice under the Residential Tenancies Act, Housing365 helps assemble the claim file, and the insurance partner assesses coverage against the policy terms.

faqItems.question: Do I need rent guarantee if I screen carefully?
faqItems.answer: Even well-screened tenants can lose a job or face illness. Rent guarantee is a cash-flow tool, not a screening tool - the two work together.

faqItems.question: Can I buy rent guarantee after the lease is signed?
faqItems.answer: Most partner policies must be bound at or before lease signing, with the lease written to match policy terms. Post-signing coverage is limited.

tenant-insurance.title: Tenant Insurance
tenant-insurance.metaDescription: Tenant insurance coordination for India landlords: enforce the renter insurance clause, collect proof, and route applicants to vetted partner providers at lease signing.
tenant-insurance.heroLede: Housing365 enforces the tenant insurance clause at lease signing, collects proof of coverage, and routes applicants to vetted insurance partners if they need a policy. No more lease clauses that exist only on paper.
tenant-insurance.problemTitle: What goes wrong when tenant insurance is optional

problemPoints.title: Clauses that never get enforced
problemPoints.body: Many leases require tenant insurance, but fewer than half of owners actually collect proof. The clause becomes decorative.

problemPoints.title: Condo boards chase the landlord
problemPoints.body: When a tenant floods the unit below, the condo corporation chargeback hits the landlord - whose insurance deductible then spikes for years.

problemPoints.title: Liability exposure on shared systems
problemPoints.body: In multi-unit buildings, a tenant-caused fire or leak can generate claims far beyond the tenant's ability to pay - unless they carry adequate liability coverage.

problemPoints.title: Tenants buy the wrong product or none at all
problemPoints.body: Without guidance, tenants pick minimum-deductible policies that do not actually cover the risks the lease is worried about.

tenant-insurance.solutionLede: Tenant insurance is treated as a gating requirement at lease signing, not an afterthought. We enforce the clause, collect the policy, and verify the coverage matches what the lease asks for.

scope.title: Lease clause enforcement
scope.body: Tenant insurance requirement drafted into the lease rider with minimum liability coverage amount and proof-of-coverage deadline.

Owners whose liability exposure from one tenant can affect the entire building.

faqItems.question: Does India law require tenants to carry insurance?
faqItems.answer: India law does not mandate tenant insurance, but landlords are permitted to require it in the lease. Most condo corporations require it on tenanted units.

faqItems.question: What coverage should I require?
faqItems.answer: A typical requirement is tenant contents coverage plus personal liability of at least $1M - and $2M for condos or multi-unit buildings. We draft the clause with you.

faqItems.question: What if the tenant refuses to buy insurance?
faqItems.answer: If the lease requires insurance and the tenant cannot produce proof, key handover is held until they do. In practice, almost every applicant complies once told it is non-negotiable.

faqItems.question: Can the landlord be named on the tenant policy?
faqItems.answer: Some partner policies allow the landlord to be named as additional insured for liability. We can request this where the partner permits.

faqItems.question: Does tenant insurance cover my building?
faqItems.answer: No. Tenant insurance covers the tenant's own contents and liability. The building itself is covered by your landlord or condo corporation policy.

faqItems.question: Do you sell the insurance?
faqItems.answer: No. Housing365 is not an insurance broker. We route applicants to vetted partner providers and coordinate proof collection.

faqItems.question: What happens at renewal?
faqItems.answer: We track policy expiry in the portal and remind the tenant in advance. If coverage lapses, you are notified.

faqItems.question: Is this the same as rent guarantee?
faqItems.answer: No. Tenant insurance protects the tenant and limits landlord liability. Rent guarantee protects the landlord's rent income. See the Rent Guarantee page for the income-protection product.

tenant-guarantor.title: Tenant Guarantor
tenant-guarantor.metaDescription: Structured guarantor and co-signer qualification for India landlords. Add a qualified co-signer to the lease with documented screening and clear liability terms.
tenant-guarantor.heroHeadline: A structured path for strong tenants who need a co-signer
tenant-guarantor.heroLede: When an applicant is a good fit but does not quite meet income or credit thresholds alone, a qualified guarantor can bridge the gap. Housing365 runs a structured guarantor screen with clear liability documentation - not an informal handshake on the rider.
tenant-guarantor.problemTitle: What goes wrong with ad-hoc guarantor arrangements

problemPoints.title: Un-screened guarantors are worthless
problemPoints.body: A guarantor signature on a rider means nothing if the guarantor has no income or assets. Without a documented screen, the owner has a signature and no recourse.

problemPoints.title: Ambiguous liability language
problemPoints.body: Many owner-drafted guarantor clauses are unenforceable because they do not specify scope, duration, or joint-and-several liability.

problemPoints.title: Out-of-province guarantors complicate enforcement
problemPoints.body: A guarantor in another province or country can be practically uncollectable even with a strong document - unless it is structured correctly.

problemPoints.title: Owners default to "no" and lose a good tenant
problemPoints.body: Without a clean guarantor process, many owners reject applicants who only needed a co-signer - and the unit sits vacant longer than it needed to.

tenant-guarantor.solutionTitle: How Housing365 runs the guarantor process
tenant-guarantor.solutionLede: The guarantor is treated like a co-applicant: same screen, same documentation, same risk summary. The guarantor rider is written with clear joint-and-several liability language and signed alongside the lease.

scope.title: Guarantor qualification screen
scope.body: Credit check, income verification, and employment verification on the guarantor - same rubric as the primary applicant.

scope.title: Income threshold validation
scope.body: Combined tenant + guarantor income mapped against your rent-to-income rule; documented in the risk summary.

scope.title: Jurisdiction check
scope.body: Where the guarantor resides assessed for enforcement practicality; flagged if out-of-country.

scope.title: Guarantor rider drafting
scope.body: Province-compliant guarantor rider with explicit joint-and-several liability, scope (rent only, or rent plus damages), and term (lease term and any renewals).

scope.title: Independent legal advice acknowledgement
scope.body: Guarantor acknowledges independent legal advice or waives it in writing - a clause that stiffens enforceability.

scope.title: E-signature execution
scope.body: Guarantor signs alongside the tenant through the Housing365 portal; all signatures captured with timestamp and IP audit trail.

faqItems.question: When does a guarantor make sense?
faqItems.answer: When the applicant fits the unit and the lifestyle but does not independently meet the rent-to-income or credit threshold - commonly students, new-to-India professionals, or early-career applicants.

faqItems.question: Do I have to accept a guarantor?
faqItems.answer: No. You decide whether to accept a guarantor arrangement. Housing365 delivers the qualified option; you approve or decline.

faqItems.question: What income level should I require from a guarantor?
faqItems.answer: A common standard is that the guarantor alone should meet the rent-to-income rule as if they were the sole tenant - typically 3x the monthly rent.

faqItems.question: Can the guarantor be in another country?
faqItems.answer: Legally permitted, but practically harder to enforce. We flag out-of-country guarantors on the risk summary so you can weigh the trade-off.

faqItems.question: What does the guarantor rider cover?
faqItems.answer: Typically joint-and-several liability for rent, and optionally for damages. The exact scope is your call and is written explicitly into the rider.

faqItems.question: Does the guarantor sign the main lease?
faqItems.answer: No. The guarantor signs the guarantor rider, which references the lease. This is standard India practice.

faqItems.question: Is the guarantor obligation limited to the initial term?
faqItems.answer: That is your choice. The rider can be written to cover only the initial term, or to extend into month-to-month and renewals. We will draft per your direction.

faqItems.question: What if the guarantor's income changes during the lease?
faqItems.answer: The guarantor rider is typically a point-in-time obligation - what matters is income at signing. Ongoing monitoring is not standard.

rental-preparation.title: Rental Preparation
rental-preparation.metaDescription: One-time rental prep for India landlords: photography, virtual tours, floor plans, paint, cleaning, junk removal, landscaping, handyman work. Listing-ready units.
rental-preparation.heroHeadline: A unit that photographs, shows, and leases
rental-preparation.heroLede: Rental Preparation is the one-time, pre-listing workstream that gets a unit ready to be photographed, marketed, and shown at top market rent. Photography and media on one side; paint, cleaning, and small repairs on the other. We coordinate every trade and produce every asset.
rental-preparation.problemTitle: What goes wrong when units are listed before they are ready

problemPoints.title: Scuffed walls and half-done cleans tank first impressions
problemPoints.body: The first 48 hours of a listing drive the majority of qualified inquiries. A unit that looks tired in photos loses those inquiries to the newer-looking unit down the block.

problemPoints.title: Phone photos cost a month of rent
problemPoints.body: A listing with amateur photos gets fewer showings, weaker applicants, and a longer vacancy - often one extra month of carrying cost versus a professionally photographed listing.

problemPoints.title: Owners juggle five trades across three weeks
problemPoints.body: Hiring a painter, a cleaner, a junk-removal crew, a landscaper, and a handyman separately means five quotes, five schedules, and a lot of weekends lost.

problemPoints.title: Deferred maintenance becomes a tenant complaint
problemPoints.body: Small issues left for the new tenant - a leaking faucet, a broken blind - start the tenancy with a service request and a bad feeling.

rental-preparation.solutionLede: One scope, one quote, one coordinator. Photography and media are produced in-house; trades are deployed from vetted partners. You approve the scope once and we deliver a listing-ready unit.

scope.title: Photography
scope.body: Wide-angle, HDR-bracketed interior photography - typically 25-to-40 delivered images per unit, colour-corrected and retouched.

scope.title: Virtual tours
scope.body: Matterport or equivalent 3D walk-through tours published alongside photos for out-of-town applicants.

scope.title: Floor plans
scope.body: To-scale floor plans with square footage, published on the listing and in the portal.

scope.title: Paint
scope.body: Touch-ups or full repaint in a neutral scheme. Ceilings, trim, and doors as needed.

scope.title: Cleaning
scope.body: Move-in ready deep clean: appliances, grout, baseboards, windows interior, and final turnover clean before photography.

scope.title: Junk removal
scope.body: Prior-tenant leftovers, basement clean-outs, and garage disposal handled by partner crews.

scope.title: Landscaping
scope.body: Lawn cut, hedge trim, and exterior tidy-up so the curb photo matches the interior.

scope.title: Handyman & small repairs
scope.body: Drywall patches, caulking, fixture swaps, blind repairs, and similar small items. Not a substitute for major renovation.

scope.title: Short-term financing support
scope.body: For larger prep budgets, we can route owners to partner financing options so prep happens before the unit sits vacant.

howItWorks.body: In-person or virtual walkthrough; we build a scope with photos and line-item recommendations.

howItWorks.title: Quote
howItWorks.body: Fixed-price quote delivered in the portal - you approve the line items you want.

howItWorks.title: Trade scheduling
howItWorks.body: All approved trades scheduled in a single timeline - typically three-to-ten days.

howItWorks.title: Work executed
howItWorks.body: Paint, clean, repairs, landscaping, junk removal executed by vetted partners and overseen by Housing365.

howItWorks.title: Media production
howItWorks.body: Photography, virtual tour, and floor plan shot after work is complete.

howItWorks.title: Listing handoff
howItWorks.body: Assets delivered to the leasing team; listing goes live within one-to-two business days of media capture.

Owners with multiple turns per year who want a repeatable, priced-in prep workflow.
Builders and developers leasing completed units who want professional media and a punch-list resolution in one pass.

faqItems.question: Is prep included in the leasing success fee?
faqItems.answer: No. Rental Preparation is a separate, optional service because scope varies dramatically from unit to unit. You approve the prep scope and price before any work begins.

faqItems.question: What does a typical prep scope cost?
faqItems.answer: A clean, paint, photo and floor-plan package for a condo typically ranges from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars depending on paint scope and unit size. We quote on the walkthrough.

faqItems.question: Do you handle major renovations?
faqItems.answer: No. Rental Preparation is listing-ready prep - cosmetic and small-repair scope. For a major renovation we can refer you to a general contractor.

faqItems.question: Can I do some of the prep myself?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Many owners paint or clean themselves and engage Housing365 for photography and media only. We will work with any subset of the scope.

faqItems.question: How long does prep take?
faqItems.answer: Typical prep runs three-to-ten business days depending on paint scope and landscaping. Media is shot at the end and the listing is launched within one-to-two days of the final photo.

faqItems.answer: Photos and media are licensed to you for use on this listing and any subsequent re-listings of the same unit.

faqItems.question: What if I need the work done fast?
faqItems.answer: Rush turns are possible in most markets. We will flag any trade with capacity risk at quote time so you can make an informed decision.

faqItems.question: Do you handle ongoing maintenance during the tenancy?
faqItems.answer: No. Ongoing maintenance is a property management function. Rental Preparation is a one-time, pre-listing scope.

institutional-lease-up.problemTitle: What goes wrong with single-agent or ad-hoc lease-ups

problemPoints.title: Absorption falls behind lender assumptions
problemPoints.body: A lender underwrote the project on a 12-month stabilization. A single leasing agent working part-time on the building will not deliver that - and the equity partner notices.

problemPoints.title: No weekly reporting to the capital stack
problemPoints.body: Developers need structured weekly reporting - showings, applicants, leases signed, rent per foot - to keep investors informed. Ad-hoc arrangements do not produce that cadence.

problemPoints.title: Rent creep decisions made too late
problemPoints.body: On a 200-unit lease-up, a pricing decision made one month late is tens of thousands of dollars in absorption opportunity. Without a data-driven pricing review each week, decisions slip.

problemPoints.title: First-tenancy quality varies unit-to-unit
problemPoints.body: Inconsistent screening across a new building creates a mixed tenant base and elevated early-tenure default rates - which hit operating ratios in year two.

institutional-lease-up.solutionLede: A deployed leasing team assigned to your building, a published rollout timeline, weekly absorption and pricing reports, and one escalation path into senior Housing365 leadership. Every unit runs through the same Leasing Services workflow - standardized applicant quality across the entire building.
